newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal ruling party wins one seat in by-elections.
newsitem.headline: Nepal ruling party wins one seat in by-elections.

text.p: Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba's ruling party on Monday won its first seat in last week's parliamentary by-elections which were swept by the communists.
The Election Commission said Keshab Bahadur Chand from Deuba's Nepali Congress party won the Baitadi One constituency in the Himalayan kingdom's far west.
Nepalis voted on Friday in the by-elections which were the first popular vote since Deuba's centrist Nepali Congress party formed a fractious coalition government in September 1995.
The opposition Communist Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) party's three victories secured its position as the single largest party in the hung parliament.
With its fresh gains, the UML has increased its position to 90 seats from 87 in the 205-member House of Representatives but still lacks the required majority to force Deuba out.
An election official told Reuters that the result of the fifth by-election in Rautahat Two parliamentary seat was expected to be announced later on Monday.
Deuba survived a no-confidence vote last month but has promised to call a confidence vote when parliament convenes next month.
Analysts said the outcome of the by-elections was crucial for Deuba's fractured three party coalition which technically commands a majority but is immobilised by fissures among its constituents.
The UML has already demanded Deuba's resignation saying that his government has lost the support of the people.
"The Prime Minister should immediately resign," UML's General Secretary Madhav Kumar Nepal told Reuters on Sunday.
Parliamentary elections are not scheduled until 1999 in the kingdom, which ushered in multi-party rule in 1990 under a constitutional monarchy after a bloody pro-democracy movement.
